chunks: And from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

A disbeliever calls out (for his needs) and Allah says, 'Hasten his wish to him,' out of aversion for his voice. And a believer supplicates for his needs and Allah says, 'Delay his wish,' out of a longing for his voice. So, on the Day of Resurrection, Allah will say (to the believer), 'You asked Me for such-and-such and I delayed answering you; so, your reward (for the delay) is such-and-such.' A believer will at that time wish any of his supplications had been never answered in the world when he sees how excellent the reward is.
ai.seo_question: Why does Allah delay the answer to a believer's prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Kitab al-Mumin* illustrates the Shia concept of *ta'khir* (delay) as a divine mercy rather than neglect, where Allah delays the believer's answer to prolong the intimacy of their supplication. The delay serves to accumulate greater reward, such that the believer, upon witnessing the magnitude of the recompense on the Day of Resurrection, wishes their prayers had remained unanswered in this world to secure that superior status.
